facts.after: Failed link fetches retain retry state. The service retries them when the backoff gate permits another attempt within the active failure window.
facts.before: An existing entry with a failed cover fetch did not retry. Metadata failures left no entry and could retry without a backoff gate.
conditions: The delay sequence is 5 minutes, 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, then 8 hours.
The retry window ends 24 hours after its first failure timestamp.
The periodic runner checks every 15 minutes, so the 5-minute gate does not guarantee a retry at exactly 5 minutes.
A legacy pending entry with no first timestamp receives a fresh window and an immediate permitted attempt.
A cover-only retry preserves successful metadata. A successful retry clears its retry fields.
The existing limit of five links per memo and ten-second enrichment deadline still applies.
The runner still scans all memos. The change also records and backfills cover dimensions.
A successful response with empty metadata remains pending. Success clears its retry timestamps, so a later pass can start a fresh window.
facts.mechanism: The enrichment service stores attempt count and timestamps. A payload runner executes at startup and every 15 minutes.

limits: This preparation did not execute the added retry tests or an application instance.
The source establishes permitted retry gates rather than exact wall-clock execution times.
The upstream plan describes legacy initialization differently from the code. The code initializes the last timestamp to zero for an immediate attempt.
No evidence establishes a success rate or operational load at scale.
The 24-hour limit applies to an active failure window. It does not bound repeated successful empty metadata responses across fresh windows.

review_evidence.scope: Pinned source facts only. Application tests and media remain outside this review.

review_requirements: An independent reviewer must verify the before and after behavior against both commits.
The reviewer must inspect all material changes in the range, not only the cited symbols.
The reviewer must confirm the evidence limits and any supplied media.
